title: Pairing and its point normalization
statement:
Let $P,Q$ be perfect $A$-complexes on $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and
let $u:P\to Q$, $v:Q\to P$, both regarded as correspondences with
support $s$. The
supported pairing satisfies

$$
\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}=\tr_A(vu\mid P),
$$

where the right-hand side is the
ordinary categorical trace.

proof.text: Use the global finite-field and finite-coefficient conventions already fixed by [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], so $k$ is algebraically closed, $A=A_{E,n}$ with $n\geq1$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. In [def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs] take $X=Y=C=D=s$, $K=P$, $L=Q$, and all legs to be identities. Thus $u:P\to Q$ and $v:Q\to P$ are an opposite pair, even when $P\neq Q$; the support intersection and all its projections are $s$ and identities. The identity functor is its own exceptional right adjoint, hence $\omega_s=A_s$ by [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Choose bounded finite-projective representatives $B,T$ of the perfect complexes, with their evaluation, coevaluation and finite dual frames as in [def-trf-categorical-trace]. Their coefficient-sheaf versions are bounded complexes of retracts of finite sums of $A_s$: their cohomology is finite constructible and their tensor products with a sheaf in degree zero have a common bounded range. They therefore belong to $D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$. All exceptional admissibility conditions in the pairing and Künneth–Verdier constructions are identity cases here. The exact equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], with the sections functor specified by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], allows us to check the morphism equality on these models. On finite sums of the unit, tensor, evaluation, and symmetry have their ordinary module formulas; restricting to the finite-projective retracts gives the signed model formulas of [def-trf-categorical-trace]. The morphism-representative bijection [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] gives degree-zero chain maps $U:B\to T$, $V:T\to B$ representing $u,v$.

source.place: first paragraph: point hypotheses and perfect-complex models

proof.text:
The class bijection is [lem-trf-correspondence-class]. For identity support it is tensor–Hom adjunction. In [def-sf-kv-maps] (ii)–(iv), all exceptional counits at the point are identity maps, and the transpose of $\kappa_{Q,P}$ is $Q\otimes P^\vee\otimes P\xrightarrow{1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_P}Q$. Its invertibility is [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier]. Choose finite dual frames $(e_{i,a},\epsilon_{i,a})$ of $B^i$ and $(f_{j,b},\phi_{j,b})$ of $T^j$ as in [def-trf-categorical-trace], so $x=\sum_a\epsilon_{i,a}(x)e_{i,a}$ and $y=\sum_b\phi_{j,b}(y)f_{j,b}$. The inverse Künneth–Verdier classes before swapping are
$$
\widetilde u(1)=\sum_{i,a}U(e_{i,a})\otimes\epsilon_{i,a},\qquad
\widetilde v'(1)=\sum_{j,b}V(f_{j,b})\otimes\phi_{j,b}.
$$
Indeed tensor–Hom transposition of the first sends $x\in B^i$ to $\sum_a\epsilon_{i,a}(x)U(e_{i,a})=U(x)$, and transposition of the second sends $y\in T^j$ to $\sum_b\phi_{j,b}(y)V(f_{j,b})=V(y)$. Apply [lem-trf-chain-supertrace] (a) to $B,T$: the displayed evaluation and finite-dual-frame coevaluation are degree-zero chain maps, with these exact signed conventions, for bounded finite-projective complexes with arbitrary differentials. Hence their composites with $U\otimes1$ and $V\otimes1$ are chain maps. Together with their computed transposes, these are exactly the classes of $u,v$. The factor-exchange in Step 1 of [def-trf-supported-pairing] gives
$$
\widetilde v(1)=\sum_{j,b}(-1)^j\phi_{j,b}\otimes V(f_{j,b}),
$$
because $|\phi_{j,b}|=-j$ and $|V(f_{j,b})|=j$.

proof.text:
The second and third source paragraphs also record a diagonal dictionary on $X$. Let $c:C\to X\times_sX$ be an admissible correspondence, $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$, and assume all the exceptional admissibility hypotheses of [lem-trf-trace-class-diagonal-pairing], including those for the diagonal opposite pair and its trace-map comparison. Put $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ and let $f:F\to X$ be its canonical map. The cited lemma states that $\langle u,1_K\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$, and that both sides are the exceptional adjoint along $f$ of the Künneth–Verdier class, base changed to the diagonal and evaluated. With $\widetilde u:Rc_!A_C\to K\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK$ defined in [def-trf-supported-pairing], this is
$$
Rf_!A_F\simeq L\Delta^*Rc_!A_C
\xrightarrow{L\Delta^*\widetilde u}K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_K\circ\operatorname{sym}}\omega_X.
$$
The first isomorphism is the fixed-square base change included in that lemma's adjoint description, and $\operatorname{ev}_K:D_XK\otimes K\to\omega_X$ is the evaluation defined in [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Thus the displayed consequence uses the existing lemma's statement, under its full hypotheses.
